h1: Suwanna Riverside Resort Chai Nat — a Chao Phraya riverside resort with cave-themed rooms and a pool
intro: If you want a place in Chai Nat that genuinely sits on the Chao Phraya River, with a pool to cool off in and an atmosphere unlike the usual tower hotels — Suwanna Riverside Resort is a name that keeps coming up. It's a boutique riverside resort in Ban Gluay subdistrict, Mueang Chai Nat. The hook is the rooms decorated with a natural cave-rock-and-waterfall theme, an outdoor riverside pool, and a boat for cruising the Chao Phraya. Rates start at about ฿780/night. The trade-off is the very distinctive styling, which some guests love and others find a little dated.

body.html: What sets Suwanna Riverside Resort apart from other places to stay in Chai Nat is that it genuinely sits on the Chao Phraya River. The resort is down a quiet riverside lane in Ban Gluay, not far from the town centre, with a stretch of riverbank to sit on, catch the breeze and watch the river and boats go by. Rare for accommodation around here, it has an outdoor riverside pool with a kids' pool too — good for families who want the children to get in the water.

The other signature here is the natural-themed room decor. Many rooms are designed to look like a cave, with faux rock walls and waterfall-style touches. If you like a quirky atmosphere that's nothing like an ordinary hotel, it's fun and photogenic. Rooms are spacious with large bathrooms, and there's a range to choose from — Standard, Superior and Family, up to Deluxe River View and Deluxe Pool Access, which lets you step straight down to the pool from your room.

On site there's the riverside Riverside Kitchen restaurant where you can eat looking out over the water, plus a Chao Phraya river-cruise service (the Charoen Sri Nava boat) for larger groups. There are also banquet and seminar rooms, so locals often use it for weddings and functions. Free parking, Wi-Fi and a 24-hour reception round things out.
"Really spacious room, big bathroom, quirky cave-style decor, attentive staff, right on the river for the atmosphere, and a pool for the kids to swim in — good value at this price."

To be straight about it, the most common complaint in the reviews is the dated styling and facilities. The cave-rock theme that some guests love makes others feel the rooms look dark and old-fashioned. A few reviews mention curtains or linens that look worn, a musty bathroom smell, and a bathroom layout where the fixtures sit awkwardly — especially for taller guests.

A couple more things to set expectations: cleaning and upkeep aren't always consistent. Some guests get a tidy room, others run into a room that wasn't fully cleaned. Reviews mention slippery bathroom floors, loud air-con units, and some staff who have limited English. If your room doesn't feel right on arrival, ask the front desk to switch you straight away.

Overall, Suwanna Riverside Resort scores 7.4 out of 10 on Trip.com from around 12 real reviews (and 3.4/5 on TripAdvisor). It's a good fit for anyone who wants a Chao Phraya riverside atmosphere, a pool, and quirky rooms on a modest budget. Rates start around ฿780 and rise with the season and room type to roughly ฿1,000 and up for a river-view or pool-access room. If you can take the distinctive styling and some dated touches, it offers a riverside setting you simply won't get in an in-town tower hotel.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Suwanna Riverside Resort Chai Nat

faq.q: Where is Suwanna Riverside Resort in Chai Nat, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Suwanna Riverside Resort is at 878 Moo 4, Soi 7, Rim Mae Nam Chao Phraya Road, Ban Gluay, Mueang Chai Nat. It sits down a quiet lane right on the Chao Phraya River, about 5 minutes from Chainat Narin Hospital and roughly a 12-minute drive to the town centre. The Chao Phraya Dam and Chai Nat Bird Park are 15-20 minutes away.

faq.q: How much does Suwanna Riverside Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿780/night for a Standard Room. Choices run from Standard, Superior and Family up to Deluxe River View and Deluxe Pool Access. Prices rise with the season and room type to roughly ฿1,000 and up for a river-view or pool-access room — always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Suwanna Riverside Resort have a pool and parking?
faq.a: Yes to both. There's an outdoor riverside swimming pool with a kids' pool, plus free parking. The riverside pool is rare for accommodation in Chai Nat and makes it a good choice for families who want the children to swim.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Suwanna Riverside Resort — are they clean?
faq.a: Rooms are spacious with large bathrooms and a distinctive natural cave-rock-and-waterfall theme. However, cleaning and upkeep aren't consistent across every room — some can look dated, with worn curtains or a musty bathroom. Check your room on arrival and ask to switch if it's not right.

faq.q: Who is Suwanna Riverside Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for anyone who wants a Chao Phraya riverside atmosphere, a pool, and quirky rooms, especially families travelling with kids. If you prefer clean, modern, minimal rooms, the cave-rock theme may feel a little dated — consider another in-town resort instead.

faq.q: Does Suwanna Riverside Resort have a restaurant and a river cruise?
faq.a: Yes. There's the riverside Riverside Kitchen restaurant where you can eat looking out over the water, plus a Chao Phraya river-cruise service (the Charoen Sri Nava boat) for larger groups. There are also banquet and seminar rooms, so locals often use it for weddings and functions.
